title: 89 Integrated fetal testicular transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles during maternal nutrient restriction with dietary melatonin intervention
content:
Abstract
Our objective is to investigate the effect of maternal nutrient restriction and melatonin supplementation on fetal testicular tissue transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles. Fetal development is imperative to ensure proper reproductive development and advancement of herd genetics and epigenetics. Maternal nutrient restriction in cattle may negatively impact development of fetal testis and subsequent fertility of offspring. It is imperative that beef cattle producers recognize the potential impact of nutritional plane to maximize efficiency and prevent financial losses. Previous studies have linked genomic instability and circadian cycle disturbances, including epigenetic changes to melatonin, a primary regulator of the circadian rhythm. On day 160 of gestation, 17 male-bearing Brangus heifers (bred to a single sire via artificial insemination) were assigned to one of the four groups in a 2 x 2 factorial treatment arrangement: adequately fed (ADQ-CON; 100% NRC recommendation, n=3), nutrient restricted (RES-CON; 60% NRC recommendation, n=5), and ADQ or RES supplemented with 20 mg/d of melatonin (ADQ-MEL, n=5; RES-MEL, n=4). On day 240 of gestation, heifers underwent cesarean sections to harvest fetuses. Fetal testicular tissue was collected and submitted to Zymo Research Corp for determination of DNA methylation and RNA transcriptome analysis. All data were analyzed and validated using R 4.2.3. In the comparison of RES-CON with ADQ-CON testicular tissues, there was no differential gene expression or methylation identified. Expression of KYAT1 gene (involved in tryptophan A.A. degradative pathway as melatonin precursor) was increased in the ADQ-MEL relative to the ADQ-CON group (adjusted p-value < 0.05) without alterations in methylation. Interestingly, a comparison between RES-MEL and RES-CON revealed 9 genes exhibiting greater expression in the RES-MEL (adjusted p-value < 0.05). Among those genes, only DAAM1 gene was hypomethylated in RES-MEL relative to RES-CON, with absolute methylation difference value of -0.21. DAAM1 is a cytoskeleton-associated protein that has a role in spermatogenesis. Conversely, 13 genes exhibited greater expression in the RES-CON vs. RES-MEL. Lastly, 5 genes exhibited increased expression in RES-MEL relative to ADQ-MEL (adjusted p-value < 0.05), among them was histone H2B (chromatin modifications), potentially leading to differential methylation on chromosome 23. Additionally, two genes (PTPRU, TDRD10) exhibited elevated expression in ADQ-MEL vs. RES-MEL (adjusted p-value < 0.05). In conclusion, dietary melatonin supplementation to nutrient restricted dams may influence fetal development as epigenetic and transcriptome regulators.
